question: A can do a piece of work in 55 days. He works for 20 days and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 49 days How many days will both take together to complete the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by A in 20 days = 20 ÷ 55 = 4/11.

Remaining work = 1 − 4/11 = 7/11.

Time taken by B for total work = 49 × (11/7) = 77 days.

Time taken by both together = (A × B) ÷ (A + B) = (55 × 77) ÷ (55 + 77) = 4235 ÷ 132 = 385/12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 385/12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 55 days

Days worked by A = 20 days

Time taken by B to finish remaining work = 49 days

**Formula Used:**

Work Done = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A in 20 days = 20/55 = 4/11 of the total work

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 4/11 = 7/11 of the total work

⇒ Time taken by B alone to complete the whole work = 49 × (11/7) = 77 days

Now, finding the total work by taking LCM of days taken by A and B.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 55
 385
 7
 
 

 B
 77
 5
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B = 7 + 5 = 12 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and B together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 385/12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 385/12 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total Work is universally assumed as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual times. This makes the calculation of daily efficiency an integer value, which significantly simplifies further calculations.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If multiple individuals work for the same number of days, their wages are simply distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns Connection

Pipes and Cisterns work on the exact same logic as Time & Work. The only difference is that a filling pipe has a positive efficiency, while an emptying pipe (or a leak) has a negative efficiency.

Combined Time Formula

If two individuals A and B can complete a task individually in 'x' and 'y' days respectively, their combined time to finish the same work together is directly given by (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.
